source.title: Predicting Memorization Within Large Language Models Fine-Tuned for Classification
source.authors: J. Dentan; Davide Buscaldi; A. Shabou; S. Vanier

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and supplement; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how early-training predictors identify samples that are memorized at completion, including experiments on a CIFAR-10 convolutional network. This is a related memorization/generalization study, but it does not test the listed generalization-gap versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's own results concern prediction of membership-inference memorization, not whether fitting random labels coexists with natural-label generalization, test error across model widths or training recipes, or removal of memorized examples. CIFAR-10 OOD canaries are used as a memorization definition, not as a random-label generalization test. The cited Zhang et al. and other prior-work results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: Section 2.3 cites prior findings about memorization and generalization, but the study's own experiments evaluate early prediction of membership-inference vulnerability. They do not test any listed version. Neither the CIFAR-10 canaries nor the supplementary training/test curves establish the comparisons or interventions those versions require.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that early-training metrics predict final memorization in classification fine-tuning, outperform their adapted baseline at an estimated 50-fold computational saving, and transfer successfully to a vision model trained from scratch.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes pretrained 7B LLMs with LoRA for classification and trains a WRN16-4 from scratch on CIFAR-10. Its intervention and outcomes concern early prediction of memorization, rather than the listed generalization-gap claims.
record.method_sensitivity: Predictor metric, threshold τ, measurement layer λ, timing ρ, memorization threshold η, dataset/model combination, and memorization definition affect reported prediction performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Early PSMI, loss and logit gap predict final LiRA-defined memorization. On MMLU/Gemma, their AUCs are 77.6%, 77.2% and 76.8%, respectively (Section 5.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early-training metrics can predict which classification training examples will later be strongly vulnerable to membership inference.

fits_no_version.finding: On WRN16-4 trained on CIFAR-10, prediction after four of 300 epochs yields AUCs of 0.85–0.87 for LiRA-defined memorization and 0.88–0.96 for designated OOD canaries (Figure 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early memorization predictors transfer to a convolutional image classifier trained from scratch.

fits_no_version.finding: Global LiRA scores and counterfactual memorization have Spearman correlations above 0.75 across tested settings, reaching 0.88 on ARC/Mistral (Supplement A.3). This measures agreement between memorization definitions, without testing the accuracy effect of removing memorized examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global membership-inference vulnerability and counterfactual memorization rank examples similarly in the tested classification settings.

record.peer_reviewed: European Conference on Artificial Intelligence (ECAI 2025; accepted for publication as stated)
record.problems: Experiments cover five dataset/model combinations, use one training epoch for the LLM fine-tuning experiments, and report many outcomes in figures. The CIFAR-10 experiment is one WRN16-4 setting. Memorization is operationalized using LiRA thresholds or OOD canaries, rather than the generalization gap in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the study does not report an outcome measuring any version's named behavior.

untested.parts: No comparison of fitting fixed random labels versus natural labels and their respective held-out accuracies.
No width sweep measuring test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks or intervention on local connectivity.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
No dropout or joint dropout/weight-decay intervention measuring held-out error.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of its ranking of generalization gaps.
No removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples followed by retraining and test-accuracy measurement.

record.verdict_notes: Keeping the result rows empty is appropriate for V1–V8. Supplementary Figure 9 reports natural-label training and test performance, but supplies none of the comparisons needed to test these versions.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No network-width sweep or test-error measurement around interpolation.
No removal of memorized training examples and retraining to measure test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
